title: OpenAI and Anthropic Set Up ‘War Rooms’ to Fight Disinfo About Midterm Elections
partialText: OpenAI, Anthropic and other tech companies have vowed to protect Tuesday’s elections from efforts to undermine democracy.

title: Gaming Out the Prospect of a Blue Wave
partialText: Business executives and investors are preparing for a Democratic sweep and the ramifications for policy on data centers, cryptocurrency and more.

title: How Broadcast, Cable and Late-Night Shows Plan to Cover the Midterm Elections
partialText: Viewers will be flooded with options, including 13 straight hours of NBC footage and a continuous livestream of Steve Kornacki and his big board.

title: The Soaring Cost of Diesel Is Bankrupting Small Trucking Companies
partialText: For small trucking firms operating with little margin for error, high fuel costs can make the difference between survival and bankruptcy.

title: For Iowa Journalist Laura Belin, Covering Politics Is a Constant Battle
partialText: Laura Belin is an openly liberal journalist in Iowa who has long been shut out by state Republican officials. Now she’s being bypassed by Democrats who favor friendly internet influencers.

title: Flouting Consumer Law, Insurers Refuse to Pay Medical Bills for Emergency Care
partialText: A law to end surprise medical bills has generated millions of high-dollar payouts for doctors. Health plans are now fighting back by frequently withholding money.

title: Saudi Aramco Profit Jumps Despite Damaging Attacks on Pipelines and Refineries
partialText: Saudi Arabia’s state-owned oil company posted a 9 percent increase in third-quarter profit on Tuesday.

title: William Nordhaus Dies; Nobel Winner Influenced Climate Policy.
partialText: The Yale professor moved climate change into mainstream economic analysis.

title: Trump Administration Said to Plan Rolling Back Pregnancy-Related Job Protections
partialText: The Biden era law was meant to help women stay in the workplace, but some conservatives say rules to enact it went too far with coverage for abortion and fertility treatment.

title: Are Freezers Being Hacked? Europe and the U.S. Military Investigate.
partialText: A wave of disruptions at grocery stores, which some officials blame on cyberattacks, highlights the vulnerability of supply chains. Shops across Europe were affected again on Monday.

title: William Nordhaus Pioneered Putting a Price on Pollution
partialText: Economist William Nordhaus said putting a price on pollution was the best way to reduce climate change. Then came the fossil fuel lobby and the anti-tax movement.

title: Trump’s Tariffs Are On the Ballot in Michigan
partialText: The levies as well as trade fighting with Canada are facing a test in the state, where voters appear skeptical of free trade but also of the president’s erratic approach.

title: Anthropic Reveals $17 Billion in Revenue as I.P.O. Approaches
partialText: The A.I. company’s quarterly revenue totaled $17 billion, 12 times as high as the same quarter last year, while its net loss totaled $23 billion.

title: How A.I. Is Making It Easier Than Ever to Microtarget Voters
partialText: Hyper-personalized messages, delivered with A.I.-enabled precision, herald a new frontier for voter outreach (and potential disinformation).

title: Martha Stewart Apologizes for Homeless Halloween Costume
partialText: Stewart, the media mogul and entrepreneur, had posted a photo of a costume with tattered clothes and a sign asking for help.

title: Cracks in the A.I. Borrowing Binge
partialText: Investors are growing increasingly concerned about the debt-fueled spending spree at the heart of the artificial intelligence buildout.

title: How The New York Times Is Covering the Midterm Elections
partialText: More than 400 journalists across at least 30 states will interview voters, break down results and identify trends.

title: Disneyland’s Autopia Ride Will Switch to Electric Vehicles
partialText: The gas-powered engines in Disneyland’s Autopia ride weren’t properly certified. The little cars will be replaced by E.V.s.

title: Gulf Economies, Torn by War in Iran, Desperately Need a Return to Normal
partialText: States like Saudi Arabia and the United Arab Emirates that have worked to rebalance from a dependence on energy have seen growth plunge in a year of strife.

title: Up in the Clouds With the Pope, It’s Still Commercial
partialText: Unlike American presidents, Pope Leo XIV has no private jet, so he travels on commercial airlines, like the rest of us. Well, almost.

title: The Nation’s Oldest Road Racetrack Starts a Big, Costly Face-Lift
partialText: New owners at Willow Springs in California have major plans for the once spartan track, hoping to lure expensive supercars and their wealthy drivers.

title: FIFA Quietly Paid Millions in Gianni Infantino’s Taxes
partialText: FIFA promises to disclose its executives’ compensation. But its under-fire president received tax benefits that were never made public, according to documents and interviews.

title: After Tech Sell-Off, Investors Brace for More Market Volatility
partialText: U.S. stock markets dipped on Monday after a rocky end on Friday, and investors face more uncertainty this week.

title: Binance Reports $3.64 Billion in Outflows as It Resumes Normal Transactions
partialText: The cryptocurrency exchange saw an immediate uptick in customer withdrawals, following the theft of $6.3 billion in tokens that has been linked to North Korea.

title: How a Little-Known Company Dominated the Persian Gulf Oil Trade
partialText: South Korea’s Sinokor controls about half the tanker transits through the Strait of Hormuz, benefiting from a big bet just before the war in Iran started.

title: ACLU’s Anthony Romero Says CEOs Are ‘Ducking the Hard Issues’
partialText: Anthony Romero has led the American Civil Liberties Union since 2001. He worries that Americans have fewer rights now.

title: As Political Ad Spending Skyrockets, Broadcast TV Remains King
partialText: Even though marketers have increasingly shifted their dollars to other media, local stations are reaping a bonanza during these midterm elections. Nowhere is this is more evident than in Texas.

title: Cyril Hilsum, Who Helped Invent Flat-Panel Displays in TVs and iPhones, Has Died at 101
partialText: The man who helped develop the technology for liquid crystal displays — the screens in flat-panel televisions and laptops — has died at 101.

title: Chili’s Margaritas Rimmed With Degreaser Burn 5 People in North Carolina
partialText: Three customers and two employees were burned on and around their mouths after a granulated substance was mistaken for sugar, a health official said.

title: Judge Tosses Trump’s $10 Billion Suit Against The Wall Street Journal
partialText: The defamation suit focused on an article about a birthday note to Jeffrey Epstein. It was the president’s second attempt to claim the publication had acted with actual malice.

title: F.D.A. Warns of Tractor Wheels Snack Bar Linked to Choking Hazard
partialText: Once Upon a Farm has recalled its Tractor Wheels soft-baked bars after reports that toddlers could not breathe while eating them.

title: How Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Went Down
partialText: A war room. A global conference call. A founder who live-posted about the largest crypto heist in history. Inside a frantic 24 hours at the world’s biggest crypto exchange.

title: The New Hot Job in Law Doesn’t Require a J.D.
partialText: Big law firms, legal tech vendors, and in-house legal departments at companies like Microsoft and Nvidia are all hiring legal engineers, a new position for lawyers with A.I. skills.

title: Pick Another Protein? Americans Still Want Beef, Despite the Price.
partialText: After chicken, consumers are buying more beef, while pork, turkey and soy products remain flat.

title: The U.S. Becomes a Global Hub for Horse Racing
partialText: More horses from overseas are competing in America’s marquee events, as the sport enjoys a renaissance.

title: Why Did So Many People File Early for Social Security Last Year?
partialText: Experts point to well-publicized turmoil at the government agency last year as a potential spark.

title: What Does Running the N.Y.C. Marathon Sound Like?
partialText: Mike Dang, a 10-time marathoner and New York Times business editor, relives the unique sonic experience of running the New York City Marathon.

title: Wanted: New Central Bank Chief. Expertise and Political Acumen Required.
partialText: The looming departure of the European Central Bank’s president, Christine Lagarde, has set in motion a high-stakes search for her successor.

title: Obamacare Policies Hit Again With Steep Premium Increases for 2027
partialText: Premiums will increase an average 13 percent next year for millions of Americans, on top of an earlier steep increase. It adds to the problems facing the program, which the Trump administration has weakened.

title: Lawsuit Accuses Education Dept. of Throttling Debt Cancellation Through PSLF Program
partialText: Public servants on the brink of student debt forgiveness are facing setbacks and extensive delays. The American Federation of Teachers sued to help them.

title: Why Kalshi Wants to Repeal a 1958 Law About Onions
partialText: A law enacted after a brazen scheme to rig onion prices in the 1950s puts the vegetable, as well as box office receipts, off-limits for prediction markets.

title: Binance Was Hacked. What Protections Exist for Crypto Customers?
partialText: After a $6.3 billion hack, the company said it was going to reimburse customers who had losses.

title: Binance’s $6.3 Billion Hack Is Just the Start of a Risky New Era
partialText: The largest cyber heist in history came as attackers increasingly use artificial intelligence and other advanced techniques to steal crypto and quickly launder the funds.

title: Meta Settles Social Media Addiction Case, Avoiding Trial
partialText: The case, brought by an 18-year-old Mississippi woman and set for trial next week, was the fourth of nine bellwether personal injury lawsuits.

title: Binance Lost Over $6 Billion in Crypto Hack. Here’s What to Know.
partialText: Hackers made off with around $6 billion in digital currency in what could be the biggest crypto heist in history. Binance said it will cover the losses.

title: Binance Hack Sends Crypto Stocks Tumbling
partialText: The rout hit publicly traded crypto exchanges and fintech companies, as well as cryptocurrencies like Bitcoin.

title: The Tech Tumult Rocks Wall Street
partialText: Investors are growing nervous about the huge spending bills that tech giants are amassing to pay for their bets on artificial intelligence.

title: U.S. Oil Industry Earned Over $130 Billion in Profit During Iran War
partialText: That was almost three times as much as what businesses producing and refining oil in the United States made in the same period in 2025.

title: Tech Stocks See Worst Day Since June, Pressuring Broader Market
partialText: The Nasdaq and the S&P 500 had their worst day since June as investors worried about spending on A.I. infrastructure.

title: High Prices Haunt Trump and the GOP on Eve of the Midterms
partialText: A backlash over high prices helped Republicans capture a majority in 2024. Now, it may be the source of the party’s own undoing.
